title: Qorǵau: Evaluating LLM Safety in Kazakh-Russian Bilingual Contexts

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the safety performance and fine-grained response patterns of LLMs across low-resource (Kazakh), high-resource (Russian), and code-switched prompts to measure disparities in safety alignment and comprehension.

Evaluating models using prompts localized to the cultural and historical contexts of Kazakhstan and Russia, measuring how well models handle region-specific sensitivities compared to general, non-localized prompts.
Using direct attacks, indirect attacks, and over-sensitivity assessment prompts designed to elicit social stereotypes, discrimination, and hate speech against various groups.
Measuring the rate of unsafe responses to prompt attacks specifically targeting regional and racial issues within the context of Kazakhstan and Russia.

Testing model safety and neutrality when presented with prompts concerning politically sensitive topics, controversial historical events, and legal/human rights matters specific to the Kazakh and Russian contexts.
